questions.q_en: How many Directive Principles of State Policy were added by the 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1976?
questions.solution_en:
The 42nd Amendment Act of 1976 was a significant constitutional amendment that made several important changes to the Indian Constitution. Specifically, it added four new Directive Principles of State Policy to Part IV of the Constitution. These additions were aimed at strengthening the social and economic foundation of the Indian state and providing clearer guidance for state policies.

The Four Added Directive Principles Were:

  1. Protecting the environment and safeguarding forests and wildlife
  2. Protecting monuments and places of national importance
  3. Separating the judiciary from the executive
  4. Promoting international peace and security

questions.q_en: Which of the following is NOT a feature of the Constitution of India?
questions.solution_en:
· India follows a single citizenship system like the UK. Dual citizenship is not allowed.

· Universal Adult Franchise: Every citizen above 18 has the right to vote.

· Independent Judiciary: Judiciary functions independently from the executive and legislature.

· Blend of Rigidity & Flexibility: The Indian Constitution can be amended but is neither too rigid nor too flexible.

Thus, the correct answer is Dual Citizenship.

questions.q_en: The concept of 'Independence of Judiciary' in the Indian Constitution is taken from the Constitution of:
questions.solution_en: The concept of the independence of the judiciary in India has been influenced by the U.S. Constitution. The American system provides a strict separation of powers, ensuring that the judiciary functions independently from the executive and legislature. This principle was incorporated into the Indian Constitution to maintain an impartial and fair judiciary.

questions.q_en: Which of the following Constitutions inspired the law-making process in India?
questions.solution_en:
The law-making process in India has been primarily influenced by the British Constitution because:

  • India's Parliamentary system of government (Lok Sabha & Rajya Sabha) follows the Westminster model of the UK.
  • The bicameral legislature, the concept of Rule of Law, and parliamentary sovereignty are derived from the British system.
  • The procedure for making laws, including debates, committee reviews, and assent by the President, is inspired by the British parliamentary process.

Thus, the British Constitution played a crucial role in shaping India's legislative system.

questions.q_en: Which fundamental duty applies to you when you see your college friends start fighting with the canteen person when he passed a few anti-religious statements?
options_en: To promote harmony and the spirit of brotherhood
To value and preserve the rich heritage
To develop the scientific temper, humanism, and the spirit of inquiry
To protect and improve our natural environment
questions.solution_en: According to Article 51A of the Indian Constitution, one of the fundamental duties is "to promote harmony and the spirit of common brotherhood among all the people of India, transcending religious, linguistic, and regional or sectional diversities." This duty applies when handling conflicts based on religious sentiments.

questions.q_en: Which of the following is NOT mentioned in the Indian Constitution as a Fundamental Duty?
questions.solution_en:
To respect the elders is not a fundamental duty mentioned in Article 51A of Indian Constitution.

Fundamental duties as per article 51A are:

It shall be the duty of every citizen of India -

(a) to abide by the Constitution and respect its ideals and institutions, the National Flag and the National Anthem;

(b) to cherish and follow the noble ideals which inspired our national struggle for freedom;

(c) to uphold and protect the sovereignty, unity and integrity of India;

(d) to defend the country and render national service when called upon to do so;

(e) to promote harmony and the spirit of common brotherhood amongst all the people of India

(f) to value and preserve the rich heritage of our composite culture;

(g) to protect and improve the natural environment

(h) to develop the scientific temper, humanism and the spirit of inquiry and reform;

(i) to safeguard public property and to abjure violence;

(j) to strive towards excellence in all spheres of individual and collective activity

(k) who is a parent or guardian to provide opportunities for education to his child or, as the case may be, ward between the age of six and fourteen years.

questions.q_en: Under which article the parliament amend the constitution?
questions.solution_en: Article 368 in Part XX of the Constitution deals with the powers of Parliament to amend the Constitution and its procedure. It states that the Parliament may, in exercise of its constituent power, amend by way of addition, variation or repeal any provision of the Constitution in accordance with the procedure laid down for the purpose. However, the Parliament cannot amend those provisions which form the 'basic structure' of the Constitution.

questions.q_en: The 61st Amendment to the Constitution of india.
options_en: restricted the size of council of ministers to 15% of the number of legislative members
exempted Arunachal Pradesh from reservation for Scheduled Castes in Panchayati Raj institutions
reduced the age for voting from 21 to 18 years
questions.solution_en:
• The Sixty-first Amendment of the Constitution of india, officially known as The Constitution (Sixty-first Amendment) Act, 1988, lowered the Voting age of elections to the Lok Sabha and to the Legislative Assemblies of States from 21 years to 18 years.

• This was done by amending Article 326 of the Constitution, which concerns elections to the Lok Sabha and the Assemblies.

questions.q_en: Which of the following is mentioned in Article 1 of the Indian Constitution?
options_en: India that is Bharat as a federation of states
India that is Bharat as a parliamentary democracy
India that is Bharat shall be a Union of states
India that is Bharat as a presidential form of democracy
questions.solution_en:
Article 1 of the Indian Constitution states:

"India, that is Bharat, shall be a Union of States."

• The term "Union of States" was chosen by Dr. B.R. Ambedkar to emphasize that states cannot secede from the Union.

• Unlike a federation, where states have the right to withdraw, India is a "union", meaning states have no such right.

questions.q_en: In which of the following cases did the Supreme Court of India give a ruling that, 'in case of any conflict between the fundamental rights and the directive principles, the former would prevail'?
questions.solution_en:
• In Champakam Doraijan Case, 1951 Supreme Court of India give a ruling that, 'in case of any conflict between the fundamental rights and the directive principles, the former would prevail'

• Golaknath Case (1967): Held that Parliament cannot amend Fundamental Rights under Article 368.

• Kesavananda Bharati Case (1973): Established the Basic Structure Doctrine, limiting Parliament's power to amend the Constitution.

• Minerva Mills Case (1980): Reinforced the basic structure doctrine and held that Fundamental Rights prevail over Directive Principles if there's a conflict.

questions.q_en:
Which of the following statements are correct regarding the Supreme Court judgement on validity of 103rd Constitutional Amendment Act?

A. The Supreme Court of India's Constitutional Bench for this case consisted of 5 judges.

B. The Constitutional Bench upholds the 10% of EWS reservation with 3-2 majority.

C. As per the Supreme Court judgement, the 103rd Constitutional Amendment is valid although it is violating the Basic Structure of the Indian Constitution.
questions.solution_en:
The Constitution Bench of the Supreme Court by 3:2 majority upheld the validity of the 103rd Constitutional Amendment which introduced 10% reservation for Economically Weaker Sections (EWS) in education and public employment.

Justice S Ravindra Bhat, with whom Chief Justice of India Uday Umesh Lalit joined, authored a dissenting opinion to strike it down. According to the minority view, the amendment - by excluding backward classes - is violative of the basic structure.
questions.solution_hi:
The Constitution Bench of the Supreme Court by 3:2 majority upheld the validity of the 103rd Constitutional Amendment which introduced 10% reservation for Economically Weaker Sections (EWS) in education and public employment.

Justice S Ravindra Bhat, with whom Chief Justice of India Uday Umesh Lalit joined, authored a dissenting opinion to strike it down. According to the minority view, the amendment - by excluding backward classes - is violative of the basic structure.
